gaps.sentence: There are plenty ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.hint: 'plenty' is always followed by this preposition before a noun
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of + noun' is the fixed pattern; no other preposition follows 'plenty'.

gaps.sentence: ___ attempts were made to contact her.
gaps.explanation: 'Several' is used with countable plurals; 'much', 'little' and 'a great deal of' need uncountables.
'Neither of my parents is ...' is correct for two items with a singular verb; 'both/all' need a plural verb and 'none' is not used for two.

gaps.sentence: I put ___ sugar in your tea by mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'Too much' is used before uncountable nouns like sugar; 'too sugar' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.
'Far too much information' is the correct intensifier pattern; 'far much' and 'far very' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: This is ___ beautiful beach on the island.
gaps.explanation: 'The most beautiful' is the superlative form used for comparisons within a group.

gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.
